name: Holographic Die Cut Stickers
seoTitle: Holographic Die Cut Stickers Cut to Your Artwork Outline
seoDescription: Holographic die cut stickers on rainbow film, cut to the artwork edge, with white ink where colors must stay solid. Laptops, bottles, merch. Free proof.
tagline: Rainbow film trimmed to the edge of your design, so the shimmer traces the shape instead of filling a square.
quickAnswer: Holographic die cut stickers are printed on a silver film with an embossed rainbow pattern, then cut to the outline of your artwork so the shimmer follows the shape instead of filling a square. White ink underneath keeps chosen colors solid. They suit merch, laptop stickers, packaging seals and event handouts. From $0.30 per sticker, 100 minimum, 5 to 7 business days production after proof approval.
highlights: Material: holographic vinyl film, white ink underprint

sections.h2: What the cut line adds to a holographic sticker
sections.html:
Put a square holographic sticker next to one cut to its outline and the difference shows from across a table. On the square, the rainbow fills the background and competes with the artwork. On the die cut piece, the film only exists where the drawing is, so every edge of the character, logo or lettering catches light and the shape does the work. That is what this page covers: holographic film contour cut to your art, with a thin border of bare film or a printed color border, supplied as individual pieces on a backing.

The sibling is our custom holographic stickers page, which is the material page: squares, circles, rolls and kiss cut sheets, plus holographic labels for packaging lines. Go there to decide if holographic film is right at all and how colors behave on it; the custom holographic sticker page covers that ground. Come here once the shape is settled and you want the cut line, the border and the white ink layer worked out for a shaped piece. The jobs we see most are artist merch, band and brand logos for laptops and water bottles, mascot stickers for events, and limited-edition seals on boxes.

sections.h2: Borders, white ink and the parts that should shimmer
sections.html:
Three decisions shape how a die cut holographic sticker looks, and the proof is where you make them.

  • Border width. We cut about 0.0625 inches outside the artwork by default. Widen it to 0.125 inches if you want a visible rainbow halo around a dark design.
  • White ink under the colors. Ink on holographic film is translucent, so a red printed straight onto it shimmers pink. White underneath makes it a flat, true red. Most logos get white under the colors and bare film in the background or outlines.
  • Bare film as a color. Leave an area unprinted and it reads as liquid silver that shifts with the light. Chrome lettering, a halo, a crown, a wave: these work best unprinted.
  • Black. Solid black over the film kills the shimmer in that spot, which is useful for text that has to stay readable.
  • Fine detail. Keep text at 7 point or larger and lines at 0.5 point or thicker; the pattern under the ink makes tiny type look busy.

Send a PNG with a transparent background or a vector file, and tell us which areas should stay bare. If you are not sure, we set it up the way we would for our own shop and show it on the free proof.

sections.h2: How holographic die cut stickers read on common surfaces
sections.html:
Holographic film is a vinyl, so it bonds to the same smooth surfaces as our white vinyl stickers, and it sits alongside clear, metallic and glow films in our sticker types catalog. What changes from surface to surface is how much the shimmer shows and how much white ink you need.

One caution: holographic shows trapped air more than white vinyl because the film is thin and reflective. Apply to a clean, dry surface and press from the center out.

sections.h2: From artwork to proof in five steps
sections.html:
1. Send the artwork as AI, EPS, SVG, PDF or a 300 dpi PNG with a transparent background, at the final size or larger.
  2. Tell us the size in inches, the quantity, and gloss or matte laminate. Gloss keeps the rainbow at full strength; matte softens it to a pearl look.
  3. Say which areas should stay bare film and which should print over white. A note such as "crown bare, text white under" is enough.
  4. We build the white ink layer, draw the cut line in magenta on the free digital proof, and simulate the film so you can judge the look.
  5. Approve the proof. Production runs 5 to 7 business days, and FedEx delivery is free within the United States, 8 to 10 business days in total.

A monitor cannot show a pattern that shifts with the viewing angle, so the proof is a guide, not a photograph. For a large run tied to a product launch, order 100 first and look at them under your own shop lights before committing to 5,000.

sections.h2: Durability: laptops, bottles, sun and the car wash
sections.html:
Every holographic die cut sticker we ship is laminated. The film itself does not fade, but the ink printed on it sits on a slick surface and needs the laminate to resist fingernails, keys and dishwashers. With gloss laminate, expect the sticker to outlast a laptop and to handle hand washing and a top-rack dishwasher cycle on a bottle. Outdoors, plan on two to three years on a vertical surface before the printed colors soften; the shimmer lasts longer than the ink.

Heat is the one thing to respect. Holographic film is thinner than our standard white vinyl and will stretch under a heat gun, which distorts the pattern. Apply at room temperature and let it cure 24 hours. For a large vehicle graphic in solid colors, where you want years of outdoor life and transfer-tape application, our die cut decal range in cut vinyl is the better build; holographic earns its keep on smaller pieces that get looked at up close.

The minimum is 100 stickers per design, and pricing starts from $0.30 per sticker; a 2 inch logo at 500 pieces lands near the low end, and larger pieces or matte laminate cost more. Several sizes of the same artwork can share the 100. Stickers arrive individually cut on a paper backing, stacked flat, with a slip sheet between bundles so the film is not scuffed in transit.

Defective pieces are reprinted at no charge inside the 10 day return window; a scratched laminate or a cut line off the art counts, a color that differs from a screen does not, which is why the proof matters. Holographic is one of a dozen films we cut to shape, and the full custom sticker range on our homepage lists the rest with the same 100 minimum and timing.

faqs.q: Do holographic die cut stickers shimmer over the printed colors or only around them?
faqs.a: Both, and you choose which. Ink on holographic film is translucent, so any color printed without white underneath shimmers through. Print white under a color and it goes flat and solid. Most designs mix the two: solid colors on the logo, bare rainbow film in the border or background, and we show the split on the proof.

faqs.q: Can a holographic die cut sticker have a solid color border instead of a rainbow edge?
faqs.a: Yes. We print the border in your chosen color over a white ink layer, then cut just outside it, so the edge reads as a clean colored outline with no visible film. White borders are the most common; a black border makes the shimmer inside the shape look brighter by contrast.

faqs.q: Will holographic die cut stickers go on a curved water bottle without lifting?
faqs.a: Yes, up to about 3 inches wide on a standard bottle. The film is thin and follows a gentle curve well, but a wide sticker wrapped around a tight radius puts stress on the edges. Keep the piece narrow, apply at room temperature, press from the center outward and give it 24 hours before the first wash.

faqs.q: Are holographic die cut stickers laminated, and does the laminate dull the effect?
faqs.a: Every piece is laminated, because the ink on holographic film scratches without it. Gloss laminate is clear and leaves the rainbow at full strength. Matte laminate softens it into a pearl shimmer with less flash; it looks good on packaging and photographs without glare, but if you want maximum sparkle, choose gloss.

faqs.q: Does black print on a holographic die cut sticker still show the rainbow?
faqs.a: No. A solid black area blocks the film, so that part of the sticker looks plain black and stays readable, which is why black works well for text and outlines. A 50 percent gray or a dark tint lets some shimmer through. If you want black that shifts color, ask for a dark tint over bare film instead.

faqs.q: How small can a holographic die cut sticker be before the pattern looks busy?
faqs.a: About 1 inch is the practical floor for a shaped piece, and 1.5 to 3 inches is where the effect reads best. Below 1 inch the embossed pattern is as big as the artwork and fine type blurs into it. Keep text at 7 point or larger and give small logos a solid white underprint so they stay legible.

faqs.q: Can holographic die cut stickers be used as tamper seals on boxes?
faqs.a: Yes, with permanent adhesive. A 1.5 to 2 inch seal cut to your logo and placed across the box flap tears rather than peeling cleanly, which is what a seal should do. On kraft boxes the contrast is strongest. For glass jars we suggest a slightly larger piece so the seal wraps over the lid edge.

faqs.q: Do holographic die cut stickers survive a dishwasher on a tumbler?
faqs.a: Top-rack dishwasher cycles are fine once the sticker has cured for 72 hours, provided it has gloss laminate and sits on a smooth part of the tumbler. Hand washing is kinder over years of use. Avoid the bottom rack and heated dry on a cheap plastic tumbler, where the heat can soften the film.

faqs.q: Why does my proof not look as shiny as the real holographic die cut sticker?
faqs.a: A monitor cannot reproduce a pattern that changes with the viewing angle, so the proof shows a simulated silver effect to indicate where the bare film sits. The printed sticker will shift through more colors and look brighter under direct light. Use the proof to check cut lines, white ink areas and text, not to judge sparkle.

faqs.q: Can holographic die cut stickers be removed from a car window cleanly?
faqs.a: Yes. Warm the sticker with a hair dryer for a few seconds, lift a corner with a plastic card and peel at a low angle. Any adhesive left on glass wipes off with isopropyl alcohol. On a laptop lid the same method works; go slowly, because the thin film tears if you yank it.

faqs.q: How many holographic die cut stickers do I need to order?
faqs.a: The minimum is 100 per design, and sizes of the same artwork can be mixed to reach it. Prices start from $0.30 per sticker and depend on size, laminate and quantity, so a 2 inch logo at 500 costs far less per piece than 100 pieces at 4 inches. Ask for a quote with your size and count for the exact figure.

faqs.q: How long do holographic die cut stickers take from proof to delivery?
faqs.a: Production takes 5 to 7 business days after you approve the free digital proof, and FedEx delivery is free within the United States, so plan on 8 to 10 business days in total. The white ink layer and lamination do not add time. If you have a release date or event, mention it on the quote and we will say whether a rush is possible.
